advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a behavioral MCP-seam test: register a read tool and invoke it against a non-git root, asserting the tool returns/raises a RebarError-mapped error rather than terminating the run.
evidence: Diff commit message: 'the exit sails past it and kills the whole anyio run: the MCP server PROCESS terminates instead of the tool returning an error.'
search: `tracker_dir` — no matches in src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py; the MCP path reaches tracker_dir via _lib_gates (`src/rebar/_lib_gates.py:42` etc.), so the tool-level contract is untested.

tests referencing `_mcp_reads` that register tools exist (tests/unit/test_audit_read.py:158, test_plan_review_explain.py:51, test_read_freshness_parity.py:184) — the seam is exercisable but no test invokes a read tool against a non-git root to assert an error is returned, not a process death.

ABSENCE: search for 'not inside a git repository' across tests yields only the reads.tracker_dir and CLI cases (test_no_sys_exit_in_read_core_176d.py:49, test_config_tracker_dir.py:101); nothing at the MCP boundary.
advisory.finding: The change's central motivation — that a read-core SystemExit killed the MCP server and the fix makes the MCP tool return an error instead — has no behavioral test at the MCP seam. Existing MCP tests (tests/unit/test_audit_read.py, test_plan_review_explain.py, test_read_freshness_parity.py all call `_mcp_reads.register_read_tools`) show the seam is testable, but none exercises a read tool against a non-git root to confirm the TrackerRootError surfaces as a tool error rather than terminating the anyio run. The behavior is only guarded indirectly by a source scan.
scenarios: An MCP read tool is invoked with an explicit non-git REBAR_ROOT or after the repo vanishes mid-session — the regression the diff fixes.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the scan to also detect os._exit and `raise SystemExit`, or replace it with a behavioral probe of the read path's process-lifetime contract.
evidence: `_calls_sys_exit` matches only `f.attr == 'exit'` with `f.value.id == 'sys'` or a bare `ast.Name` `exit` (lines 168-172).
Docstring claims 'must not contain a process-terminating call' (line 181) but the matcher does not cover os._exit / raise SystemExit.
dropped.finding: test_no_sys_exit_on_the_library_read_path asserts the TEXT of the source under test (absence of a `sys.exit(...)`/`exit(...)` AST node) rather than observable behavior, and its AST matcher only recognizes `sys.exit`/bare `exit` calls — it is blind to `os._exit(...)`, `raise SystemExit(...)`, or termination via any other name, so it does not fully cover the 'library read path may not terminate its host process' contract it claims.
scenarios: A future edit reintroduces process termination via os._exit or `raise SystemExit` on a read-path module.
